planting.note: Tuck divisions into limestone rubble or crevices with sharp drainage in spring, mimicking the shaded canyon walls of its native Edwards Plateau range rather than a rich garden bed.

directions: Manyflower alumroot is endemic to shaded limestone canyon walls and grottoes of the Texas Edwards Plateau, where it roots into thin, alkaline rock crevices rather than ordinary soil. Its species name refers to the tightly clustered (glomerulate) small flowers it carries on wiry stems, a denser arrangement than the loose, open flower sprays typical of most other alumroots. Once established on sharply drained, calcareous ground it tolerates the region's hot, dry summers well, making it a good fit for limestone rock gardens, dry shaded walls, or trough plantings that recreate its native canyon habitat. Avoid rich, moisture-retentive soil, which encourages crown rot in this lean-site specialist.
sources: Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center Native Plant Database
